subject: exercise-sports-science
title: Energy Systems: Three Systems Sharing One Bout

questions.prompt: During one continuous bout of exercise, how do the three energy systems supply energy?

choices.text: Only ATP-PC works at first, then it switches off and glycolysis works alone
The aerobic system stays off until the other two run out, then it works alone
All three systems are active from the first second and overlap throughout the bout, with only the largest contributor changing
Each system works alone for exactly the same length of time before handing over

questions.misconception: The body uses only one energy system at a time and switches cleanly to the next one when the first runs out.
questions.explanation: The trap claim is: The body uses only one energy system at a time and switches cleanly to the next one when the first runs out. In fact All three systems are active from the first second and overlap throughout the bout; only the largest contributor changes as the bout continues - ATP-PC fades as the phosphocreatine store drains, anaerobic glycolysis peaks as lactate builds, and the aerobic system rises to dominate longer work.

questions.prompt: In the first seconds of the bout, which system holds the largest share, and how large is it?

choices.text: ATP-PC, at 70 percent, while the phosphocreatine store is full
All three systems hold an equal share

questions.explanation: Scene 1 works this: all three systems switch on together, and ATP-PC holds the largest share at 70 percent in the first seconds, ahead of glycolysis at 20 percent and the aerobic system at 10 percent.

questions.prompt: A student says the body uses only one energy system at a time and switches cleanly to the next one. Explain, in two sentences, what actually happens to the three systems during the bout.
questions.answer: All three systems are active from the first second and overlap throughout the bout; only the largest contributor changes as the bout continues - ATP-PC fades as the phosphocreatine store drains, anaerobic glycolysis peaks as lactate builds, and the aerobic system rises to dominate longer work.
questions.explanation: The deciding habit is to track all three shares at once: each system contributes at every stage, and only the identity of the largest contributor changes as the bout continues.

questions.prompt: In one sentence, state the share of each system at about 30 seconds and check the total.
questions.answer: At about 30 seconds ATP-PC supplies 10 percent, anaerobic glycolysis 55 percent and the aerobic system 35 percent, and the three shares sum to 100 percent.
questions.explanation: Scene 3 shows glycolysis holding the largest share at 55 percent as lactate builds, with the aerobic share climbing to 35 percent and ATP-PC down to 10 percent but not zero.

questions.prompt: Which list gives the stages of the bout in order?

choices.text: All three switch on together with ATP-PC at 70 percent, ATP-PC fades to 35 percent as the store drains, glycolysis peaks at 55 percent as lactate builds, the aerobic system ramps up to 75 percent
ATP-PC works alone, then switches off, glycolysis works alone, then switches off, the aerobic system works alone
The aerobic system dominates first, glycolysis peaks, then ATP-PC takes over at the end
Glycolysis peaks at 55 percent, all three switch on together, the aerobic system ramps up, ATP-PC starts at 70 percent

questions.explanation: Scene 1 switches all three systems on together, scene 2 fades ATP-PC as the phosphocreatine store drains, scene 3 peaks glycolysis as lactate builds, and scene 4 ramps the aerobic system up to dominate.
